Panama’s government has declared a state of emergency on Saturday as the aftershocks of two powerful earthquakes that roiled the country shook communities for hours.

Officials did not attribute any deaths to Friday’s 7.7- and 6.6-magnitude earthquakes, but reported damages in all 10 of Panama’s provinces and two Indigenous territories.

The 45-year-old, who shares two of his names with the notorious European dictators, won the race for mayor of Queropalca, in Peru’s central Huánuco region, and will take office on 1 January.

Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week.

rfi.title: Chinese carmakers descend on Paris as battle for European market intensifies
rfi.description: A record 20 Chinese car brands are expected at the opening of the Paris Motor Show on Monday, as Europe's car industry faces growing competition and struggles to keep pace with the shift to electric vehicles.

rfi.title: Glucksmann wins French left primary to run as alternative to Melenchon
rfi.description: Centre-right politician Raphael Glucksmann has won France’s primary of the left to become the its candidate in next year's presidential elections, positioning himself as the centre-left’s main alternative to hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon in the face of the rise of far right leader Marine Le Pen.

rfi.title: France urges Palestinians to reverse decision on delayed elections
rfi.description: France on Sunday called on Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to reverse a decision to postpone legislative elections, originally set for 28 November. Abbas said on Saturday that due to "Israeli obstacles", the vote would be held in September next year, alongside a presidential poll.

rfi.title: Western leaders slam Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, warn citizens to stay away
rfi.description: UN and EU leaders voiced shock and anger on Sunday following an attack by Yemen's Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia and warned against an escalation in the deadly conflict. Several embassies have issued warnings to their citizens to avoid the area.

rfi.title: Rescuers search for missing migrants after deadly boat wreck off Djibouti
rfi.description: The death toll from a boat sinking off the shores of Djibouti on the night of 8-9 October, has risen to at least 139, a UN agency said Sunday, after 30 more bodies were found. Rescue operations are underway to find the dozens of missing. More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.

rfi.title: Climate lawsuits gain ground as governments scale back climate action
rfi.description: The political fight against global warming may be losing steam, but the legal battle is heating up. Over the past decade, legal activists have successfully taken a number of national governments to court, triggering the adoption of more climate-friendly policies in countries including the Netherlands, Pakistan, Switzerland, South Korea and others.

rfi.title: How Egyptian femtech is tackling taboos around women's health
rfi.description: Cultural taboos and a lack of understanding can be a barrier for women to access healthcare in Egypt, alongside the cost of treatment. But the country's budding femtech sector is creating new pathways to help and information.

rfi.title: Palestinian Mahmoud Abu Hamda wins top photography prize at Bayeux
rfi.description: Palestinian freelancer Mahmoud Abu Hamda on Saturday won the photography category in the prestigious Bayeux award for war correspondents for his work from Gaza.

rfi.title: France boss Zidane generates 'electric atmosphere' with Nations League wins
rfi.description: Zinédine Zidane was renowned for his prodigious skills during a 17-year playing career that took him from the streets of Marseille to glamorous European clubs such as Juventus and Real Madrid – as well as to a World Cup win for France in 1998. Now, as France coach, he is showing that his flair for the unexpected has not deserted him.

rfi.title: French prodigy Seixas becomes youngest Giro di Lombardia winner
rfi.description: French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas ended his breakout season as a history-making Monument winner with a "dream" victory at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday at just 20 years old.

rfi.title: EU says US deal lifting diesel sanctions 'funds' Russian war on Ukraine
rfi.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Saturday that lifting sanctions on Russian diesel helped fuel the Kremlin's war on Ukraine, after US President Donald Trump announced a deal for Moscow to supply fuel.

rfi.title: French Socialist party primary vote extended due to cyberattack
rfi.description: The first round of France's Socialist Party's primary has been extended until 6pm on Sunday after a cyberattack slowed down proceedings, organisers said. An investigation is underway.

rfi.title: French astronaut recounts 'astonishing' emotions after return to Earth
rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot has returned back to earth full of "emotion" after spending eight months in space – breaking the record for the longest uninterrupted orbital stay by a European astronaut. She will complete a recovery programme at the European Space Agency centre in Cologne, Germany before returning to France.

rfi.title: France promises more teachers and student representation but protests continue
rfi.description: France's government has promised 3,000 replacement teachers for struggling secondary schools and pledged to give pupils a greater say in education policy in a bid to quell nearly three weeks of student protests. But blockades in some schools resumed on Friday morning and student bodies have called for a further day of action next week.

rfi.title: Exiled Ukrainian women prepare for life after war, with or without returning home
rfi.description: Since the full-scale Russian invasion on February 2022, Ukrainian organisations abroad have taken on an increasingly important role in supporting their country. With women and children making up the majority of recent exiles, women's groups have a particular part to play in winning support for Ukraine – as well as making sure its cultural identity survives.

rfi.title: UN alarmed as number of displaced in central Sahel reaches nearly four million
rfi.description: The United Nations on Friday raised the alarm about a displacement crisis in the central Sahel where nearly four million people have been forced to flee their homes in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.

rfi.title: Ghana faces challenge to persuade Brics it deserves a seat at the table
rfi.description: Ghana is seeking to widen its trade and diplomatic options beyond the West by applying to join the Brics bloc of emerging economies. But a seat at the table is far from guaranteed: Ghana will have to convince all 11 existing members it is a valuable new partner.

rfi.title: A race against time to prevent an outbreak follows Kenya's first Ebola death
rfi.description: Kenya's first imported case of Ebola – in which the patient travelled from Democratic Republic of Congo via Uganda – has exposed failings in border screening processes. Now Kenyan health officials are racing against the clock to prevent one infection from becoming an outbreak.

euronews.title: EU decries 'concerning' Trump-Putin deal, insists sanctions on Russia will continue
euronews.description: The Trump-Putin diesel deal has been badly received by EU foreign ministers, who say it undermines transatlantic unity at a time when Russia intensifies its attacks on Ukraine.

euronews.title: Footage shows Glucksmann covered in flour after winning French left-wing presidential primary
euronews.description: French politician and European Parliament member Raphaël Glucksmann was pelted with flour outside a bar in Paris on Sunday evening, shortly after winning the social-democratic left’s primary for the 2027 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote.

euronews.title: CCTV shows moment of strike at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh
euronews.description: CTV footage released by Saudi authorities shows the moment a missile strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10. The attack killed at least 13 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of airport operations.

euronews.title: Judge orders Trump to pull taxpayer-funded adverts

euronews.title: France’s main problem is its inability to reduce public debt, economist says
euronews.description: French economist Nicolas Bouzou says France's economic growth is not "strong" enough to sustain the country's welfare state.

euronews.title: Tens of thousands march in Brussels demanding urgent climate action
euronews.description: Tens of thousands of people marched through Brussels on Sunday, 11 October, demanding stronger action on climate change ahead of next month's COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey.

euronews.title: Spain national day military parade: 4,380 troops, 82 aircraft and Dragón armoured vehicles debut
euronews.description: Madrid puts on its finery for the National Day of Spain parade, with general elections looming and tensions high over the housing crisis and migration pressures.

euronews.title: Opposition figures and journalists allege police abuses during India protests
euronews.description: The protests were triggered by allegations of manipulating voter lists during a nationwide roll revision that critics say could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

euronews.title: 'NATO's KPI is peace', Latvia's foreign minister says
euronews.description: Baiba Braže, Latvia's foreign minister, believes NATO's eastern flank is well protected at a time when it is facing heightened tensions. Latvia and its Baltic neighbours are once again on alert amid growing concerns over Russian drones and airspace violations.

euronews.title: Mystery of La Navidad: site of first Spanish settlement in Americas unknown
euronews.description: On Christmas Eve 1492 the Santa María ran aground off Haiti; Columbus used its timbers to build Fort Navidad, where 39 men died. More than five centuries later, archaeologists have yet to pinpoint the site.

euronews.title: Why does the EU want a European Security Council? Take our poll
euronews.description: The EU wants to build a new security mechanism to face hybrid threats, like drone incursions, cyberattacks and sabotage. But does it really need a new Security Council?

euronews.title: How can a new Security Council boost the EU's defence strategy? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
euronews.description: The EU is reviving the idea of a European Security Council as Russia's hybrid attacks continue and reliance on US commitment to NATO remains risky. But how could this look like? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

euronews.title: Rare Kandinsky masterpiece and Hockney’s beloved dog painting head to London auction
euronews.description: Around 50 works by some of the biggest names in modern and contemporary art are going under the hammer at Christie’s in London on Wednesday 14 October.

euronews.description: The prime minister said Germany’s Friedrich Merz had told him the far-right AfD was linked to Russia, as he faces questions at home over Labour’s ties to the UAE.

euronews.title: Addictive behaviour is falling among Portuguese teens but most vulnerable are still exposed
euronews.description: Portuguese teenagers are drinking and using drugs less and facing fewer problems, but risks are increasingly concentrated among those with multiple vulnerabilities, according to a new ICAD study on addictive behaviours.

euronews.title: Europe Today: Trump claims Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire as Baltics stay on alert
euronews.description: Donald Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed an energy ceasefire. Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it was news to him. As he addresses the Warsaw Security Forum, we hear from Latvia's FM Baiba Braže, Doha after a deadly Riyadh airport attack, and France's debt fears.

lemonde.description: Donald Trump a annoncé, dimanche, un cessez-le-feu sur les infrastructures énergétiques russes et ukrainiennes, sans que Kiev n’en ait été informé. Moscou s’est gardé, pour l’heure, du moindre commentaire.

lemonde.title: Mouvement lycéen : face à une violence inédite dans plusieurs établissements, des proviseurs épuisés et sur le qui-vive
lemonde.description: Si la majorité des lycées touchés par la mobilisation connaissent des blocages sans heurts, d’autres ont été le théâtre de tensions et de dégradations. Des chefs d’établissement ont aussi été blessés et menacés. Plusieurs d’entre eux racontent la difficulté à « tenir le choc » et à rouvrir les portes de leurs lycées.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann, vainqueur de la primaire à gauche, doit désormais mettre la famille sociale-démocrate en ordre de bataille
lemonde.description: Le coprésident de Place publique, qui l’a emporté dès le premier tour, dimanche, a revendiqué la « rupture avec le macronisme » et la fin de « l’hégémonie de Jean-Luc Mélenchon sur la gauche », tout en assurant que le principal adversaire reste « l’extrême droite ».

lemonde.title: Le marché des Enfants-Rouges, à Paris, « totalement détruit » après un incendie
lemonde.description: Le maire de Paris Centre, qui a annoncé l’information tôt lundi matin, a fait savoir que le feu était « maîtrisé, mais le marché, situé dans le IIIᵉ arrondissement, est « totalement sinistré ».

lemonde.title: Dorothée Gilbert, danseuse étoile à l’Opéra national de Paris : « Les adieux, on ne les prépare pas, on fait avec ! »
lemonde.description: L’artiste donne, le 15 octobre, sa dernière représentation à 43 ans, avec « L’Histoire de Manon », accompagnée d’Hugo Marchand. Dans un entretien au « Monde », elle revient sur ce moment particulier, et sur l’importance de la transmission.

lemonde.title: « Naza » : un documentaire vertigineux sur la guerre automatisée et déshumanisée d’Israël à Gaza
lemonde.description: En interrogeant des militaires israéliens, le documentaire polémique de Yuval Abraham et Rachel Szor dévoile comment les dispositifs technologiques intégrés à la machine de guerre israélienne ont normalisé les pertes civiles.

lemonde.title: Compte à terme ou livret bancaire, quel est le meilleur choix après la hausse des taux ?
lemonde.description: Certains placements sans risque font désormais mieux que le Livret A. Une situation qui devrait durer au moins jusqu’au 1ᵉʳ février 2027.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : rejeté en commission, le projet de loi de finances arrive dans le chaudron de l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Le texte, examiné dans l’Hémicycle à partir de mardi, doit permettre de tenir jusqu’à l’élection présidentielle sans crise de la dette. Mais nul ne sait s’il pourra être adopté, ni quand. En cas de blocage, Sébastien Lecornu n’exclut plus de recourir à des ordonnances.

lemonde.title: En Pologne, l’extrême droite mise en cause dans la tentative d’assassinat contre le premier ministre Donald Tusk et son ministre de la défense
lemonde.description: Un homme a été arrêté, dimanche 11 octobre, qui est lié à l’ultra-droite polonaise. A ce stade, a jugé le ministre de l’intérieur, Marcin Kierwinski, il est « trop tôt » pour établir si cette affaire revêt une « dimension internationale ».

lemonde.title: Le commissaire européen au climat compte sur le « made in Europe » et le nucléaire pour réduire les émissions de carbone
lemonde.description: Alors que la France et l’Allemagne peinent à trouver un accord politique sur le sujet, Wopke Hoekstra, en visite à Paris mardi et mercredi, soutient la position française en faveur d’une préférence européenne pour résister à la concurrence de l’industrie chinoise.

lemonde.title: Justin, 25 ans, ornithologue, 1 950 euros par mois : « Je fais une petite fixette sur les goélands »
lemonde.description: « La bonne paye ». Chaque semaine, « Le Monde » parle d’argent avec les jeunes. Que signifie « bien gagner sa vie » ? Comment se projettent-ils dans l’avenir ? Cette semaine, Justin Chambrelin raconte comment sa passion pour les oiseaux l’a mené vers son métier dans l’associatif.

lemonde.title: En Inde, les étudiantes marchent contre la « culture du viol »
lemonde.description: Les manifestations se multiplient à New Delhi pour dénoncer la faiblesse de la réponse des autorités face aux meurtres et aux viols de jeunes femmes, parfois mineures. Elles défendent la place des Indiennes dans l’espace public.

lemonde.title: « Plutôt que de démystifier le “prix Nobel d’économie”, il convient de comprendre ce qu’il récompense vraiment »
lemonde.description: Dans sa chronique, l’historienne Béatrice Cherrier analyse les critiques et commentaires qui accompagnent, depuis sa création, en 1968, le Prix de la Banque de Suède en sciences économiques en mémoire d’Alfred Nobel, dont les lauréats pour 2026 seront connus le 12 octobre.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi Ceuta et Melilla restent un sujet de discorde entre l’Espagne et le Maroc
lemonde.description: L’arrivée de plus de 72 000 migrants à Ceuta, en provenance du Maroc, les 30 et 31 juillet, a ravivé la question de la souveraineté de l’Espagne sur les deux villes autonomes de la côte nord-africaine. Une souveraineté revendiquée par Rabat depuis les années 1960, à laquelle la visite annoncée du roi Felipe VI, le 13 octobre, doit symboliquement opposer une énième fin de non-recevoir.

lemonde.title: En Roumanie, le sombre passé de la Securitate continue d’animer la scène politique
lemonde.description: Révélé par la presse en fin d’été, le cas d’un ex-officier de la Securitate qui commandait la garde rapprochée présidentielle depuis vingt ans a ravivé la défiance des Roumains envers leurs institutions, dans un contexte de crise politique. Les historiens portent un regard nuancé sur l’influence persistante des anciens des services de sécurité.

lemonde.description: Ces tirs nord-coréens surviennent quelques jours après l’essai par le Sud de son premier système de planeurs hypersoniques.

zeit.description: Alexander Schweitzer soll nach ZEIT-Informationen auf Bärbel Bas an der Spitze des Arbeitsministeriums folgen. Er ist derzeit SPD-Vorsitzender in Rheinland-Pfalz.

nzz.title: Verschärft Trump den Druck auf Russlands Schattenflotte?
nzz.description: Eigentlich sollte das Weisse Haus bald neue Massnahmen gegen die russische Schattenflotte vorlegen. Doch das Dieselabkommen mit Putin weckt Zweifel an einem solchen Schritt. Zudem setzt der Kreml alles daran, seine Öltanker abzuschirmen.

nzz.title: Der Zürichsee hat einen historischen Tiefstand erreicht. Die Folgen würden noch lange anhalten, sagt ein Experte
nzz.description: Selbst beständiger Niederschlag hilft nur bedingt, damit wieder mehr Wasser in den Zürichsee gelangt. Denn der Regen hat seine Eigenheiten.

nzz.title: Chaostage im Königreich: Die Huthi greifen den Flughafen in Riad erneut an
nzz.description: Dreizehn Menschen wurden am Samstag bei der Attacke getötet und über 300 verletzt – es ist einer der schlimmsten Angriffe in der Geschichte Saudiarabiens. Zwar demonstrieren die Bewohner von Riad Gelassenheit. Doch dem Königreich stehen schwere Zeiten bevor.

nzz.title: Afrikanische Länder glauben, Milliarden zu verlieren, weil die Wall Street sie unfair behandelt. Nun gründen sie eine eigene Rating-Agentur
nzz.description: Kaum Analysten vor Ort, kein Verständnis für informelle Märkte: Die grossen Kredit-Rating-Agenturen verstehen Afrika angeblich nicht. Deshalb gibt es nun ein afrikanisches Institut. Dieses wird die Finanzmärkte überzeugen müssen, dass es unabhängig ist.

nzz.title: «I can English understand» – warum der Bundesratsjob immer schwieriger wird
nzz.description: Im Schweizer Regierungsalltag sind internationale Kontakte und Netzwerke wichtiger denn je. Doch ein guter Bundesrat muss ganz andere Fähigkeiten mitbringen als ein Politiker in den Nachbarländern.

nzz.title: Trump stürzt das amerikanisch-ukrainische Verhältnis in eine neuerliche Krise
nzz.description: Donald Trump findet, die Ukraine brauche einen neuen Präsidenten. Das erinnert an den Eklat im Oval Office zwischen Trump und Selenski vor eineinhalb Jahren. Die Ukraine ist heute zwar weniger abhängig von amerikanischer Hilfe als damals, aber das erneute Zerwürfnis könnte schwierig werden für die Ukraine.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die rot-grüne Mehrheit in Zürich glaubt, die Stadt unter einer Glasglocke weiterentwickeln zu können. Statt Grossstadtflair herrscht Kleingeistigkeit
nzz.description: Von Wohntürmen bis zum neuen Stadtfest: Zürich will nicht mehr hoch hinaus und hält sich trotzdem für unersetzbar. Diese Hybris ist besorgniserregend.

nzz.title: Trumps Justizdepartement ermittelt gegen fünf grosse Fernsehsender, weil sie den Gipfel mit Xi Jinping nicht übertrugen
nzz.description: Der Streit nahm seinen Anfang, als die Regierung CNN den Zutritt zum Weissen Haus verwehrte und andere Fernsehsender daraufhin Anlässe des Präsidenten aus Solidarität boykottierten.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Linkspartei beharrt auf ihrem Antisemitismus
nzz.description: Die Berliner Linkspartei wehrt sich nach Kräften dagegen, judenfeindliche Äusserungen als solche zu benennen. SPD und Grüne sollten begreifen, wie radikal ihr politischer Wunschpartner ist.

nzz.title: Bürgerliche brechen Versprechen: Trotz Steuersenkung für den Mittelstand ist nun auch die Steuerbremse für Reiche zurück
nzz.description: Der Grosse Rat des Kantons Waadt hat für Wohlhabende eine vorteilhaftere Steuerbremse beschlossen. Damit widerspricht er einem früheren Entscheid.

nzz.title: Open AI schockiert die Anleger: Macht das Unternehmen viel weniger Umsatz, als die Börse glaubte?
nzz.description: Der hochgerechnete Jahresumsatz von Sam Altmans KI-Firma soll derzeit 50 Milliarden Dollar betragen und nicht 70 Milliarden, wie zuvor kolportiert wurde. Die Neuigkeit liess am Donnerstag die Aktienkurse zahlreicher Techfirmen fallen.

nzz.title: Europa sucht seinen «Elon Musk» für die Raumfahrt und glaubt, ihn in einem belgischen Ingenieur gefunden zu haben
nzz.description: Die EU gibt der Firma von Benoît Deper einen teuren Vertrauensvorschuss: Sie soll über zweihundert Satelliten bauen, um Europa bei der Kommunikation von den USA unabhängig zu machen. Dabei ist das Unternehmen erst im Aufbau.

nzz.title: Alltagsstress und Zukunftsangst: Chinas junge Generation wendet sich Mao Zedong zu
nzz.description: Mit dem Sturz der Viererbande endete vor fünfzig Jahren die Mao-Ära. Doch in wirtschaftlich unsicheren Zeiten mit immer kleineren Salären und immer grösserem Druck besinnen sich junge Menschen wieder auf die Lehren des Gründervaters der Volksrepublik.

nzz.title: Jans will den Zugang zum Asylverfahren erschweren – doch werden die Erwartungen wieder einmal zu hoch hinaufgeschraubt?
nzz.description: Wer sein Asylgesuch nicht begründet, soll gar kein Asylverfahren mehr erhalten. Das ist die Idee hinter dem vom Bundesrat in Aussicht gestellten Zuständigkeitsverfahren. Wie viel es bringt, ist unklar.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Yémen en direct : l'aéroport de Riyad encore fermé lundi après les attaques houthies
france24fr.description: Les Houthis du Yémen ont revendiqué dimanche des "opérations d'envergure" contre des aéroports et des infrastructures énergétiques saoudiennes. En réaction, le ministre saoudien de l'Énergie a exigé une réponse ferme. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: L'OM respire, Paul Seixas précoce, Gabby Williams flamboyante : les infos sport du week-end
france24fr.description: En Ligue 1, Marseille est sorti de la zone rouge grâce à un précieux succès sur la pelouse de Troyes. Plus jeune vainqueur de l'histoire du Tour de Lombardie, son premier Monument, Paul Seixas a bouclé en beauté une saison éblouissante. La basketteuse française Gabby Williams a envoyé San Francisco en finale WNBA, un nouveau sommet où elle tentera d'inscrire son nom au bout d'une irrésistible ascension.

france24fr.title: Le marché des Enfants-Rouges, à Paris, "ravagé" par un incendie
france24fr.description: Un feu a "ravagé" le marché des Enfants-Rouges, situé au cœur de la capitale, a annoncé la mairie de Paris Centre tôt lundi matin. Il s'agit du plus vieux marché couvert de Paris.

france24fr.title: Marseille s'impose difficilement à Troyes et sort de la zone de relégation
france24fr.description: C'était la victoire ou la crise pour l'OM, ce dimanche à Troyes. Relégables au coup d’envoi, les Phocéens devaient absolument s'imposer en clôture de la sixième journée de Ligue 1. C'est chose faite, grâce à des buts du Marocain Amine Harit et de l'Algérien Himad Abdelli.

france24fr.title: Raphaël Glucksmann enfariné après sa victoire à la primaire de la gauche sociale-démocrate
france24fr.description: Une personne a vidé un paquet de farine sur Raphaël Glucksmann dimanche, alors que le candidat à la présidentielle sortait d’un bar où il fêtait sa victoire à la primaire de la gauche.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'UE soutiendra une trêve énergétique entre l'Ukraine et la Russie "dès qu'elle tiendra"
france24fr.description: L'Union européenne s'est dite prête à soutenir une trêve des frappes sur les infrastructures énergétiques entre la Russie et l'Ukraine "dès qu'elle tiendra", a affirmé lundi sa cheffe de la diplomatie, Kaja Kallas. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Répression en Inde: "Les cafards survivent, nous reviendrons"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce lundi 12 octobre, la victoire, hier, en France, de Raphaël Glucksmann à la primaire sociale-démocrate dès le premier tour. La poursuite annoncée de la mobilisation des lycéens. La capitale indienne bouclée ce week-end pour empêcher un rassemblement du Parti du peuple cafard. Une double arrestation, au Liban, qui soulève beaucoup de questions. Et un appel à la grève des femmes, demain.

france24fr.title: La Corée du Nord a tiré plusieurs missiles balistiques vers la mer du Japon, selon Séoul
france24fr.description: "Plusieurs missiles balistiques" ont été tirés par la Corée du Nord vers la mer du Japon, a annoncé la Corée du Sud lundi. Ces tirs surviennent quelques jours après l'essai, par Séoul, de son premier système de planeurs hypersoniques.

france24fr.title: Plus de 29 °C : El Niño entraîne des températures inédites dans le Pacifique
france24fr.description: El Niño a entraîné le réchauffement d'une partie de l’océan à des niveaux inédits, poussant les mers du monde à des températures encore jamais atteintes pour ce mois, indique lundi l'observatoire européen Copernicus.

france24fr.title: Nascar : le phénomène français de 22 ans Paul Jouffreau en quête du titre de champion d'Europe
france24fr.description: Les 17-18 octobre 2026 aura lieu sur le circuit de Zolder en Belgique, la finale de la saison de NASCAR Euro Series, une compétition de sport automobile avec des voitures de catégorie stockcar. Le Français Paul Jouffreau au volant de sa Ford Mustang de l'écurie RDV Compétition va tenter de remporter son premier titre de champion du monde, avec deux victoires jusqu'ici. Le jeune pilote de 22 ans avait terminé 2ème et 3ème lors des deux dernières saisons.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann élu dès le premier tour de la primaire à gauche
france24fr.description: Le parti socialiste a désormais son candidat officiel pour 2027, c'est l'eurodéputé Raphaël Glucksmann. On en parle avec nos invités Emilie Zapalski, éditorialiste et communicante politique, et Noé Girardot-Champsaur, expert associé à la Fondation Jean-Jaurès.

france24fr.title: L'Érythrée accuse l'Éthiopie de déstabiliser la région
france24fr.description: La tension monte entre l'Éthiopie et l'Érythrée. L'armée éthiopienne poursuit son offensive dans le Tigré, où des troupes érythréennes auraient pénétré ces derniers jours. Les deux pays s'accusent mutuellement d'agression. Asmara dénonce une déclaration de guerre et saisit les Nations unies.

france24fr.title: Un terrain, deux acheteurs, qui est le véritable propriétaire? Focus sur le foncier en Afrique
france24fr.description:
Acheter un terrain, construire sa maison, investir les économies de toute une vie… et découvrir que la parcelle est revendiquée par quelqu'un d'autre. En Afrique, les conflits fonciers soulèvent des questions essentielles : comment vérifier qu'un vendeur est réellement habilité à céder un terrain ? Quelle différence entre un droit coutumier, une attestation et un titre foncier ? Et comment éviter les doubles ventes et les fraudes immobilières ?

spiegel.title: Private Krankenversicherung: Warum es richtig wäre, sie abzuschaffen
spiegel.description: Die meisten Menschen in Deutschland finden es ungerecht, dass Privatpatienten bevorzugt werden. Zeit für einen Systemwechsel.

spiegel.title: Bärbel Bas - Reaktionen auf ihren Rücktritt: »Die Kraft ist endlich«
spiegel.description: Bärbel Bas ist aufgrund eines Trauerfalls als Co-Vorsitzende der SPD und Bundesarbeitsministerin zurückgetreten. Parteikollegen kritisieren die CDU für Angriffe gegen Bas. Die Reaktionen im Überblick.

spiegel.title: Johann Wadepuhl: EU-Außenminister planen bislang größtes Sanktionspaket gegen Russland
spiegel.description: Außenminister Wadephul spricht von einem »beispiellosen Sanktionsschlag«: Die EU setzt 1600 Namen aus Russlands militärisch-industriellem Komplex auf die Liste. Für einige hat sich Deutschland besonders eingesetzt.

spiegel.title: Audi: Verkäufe brechen um fast ein Fünftel ein
spiegel.description: Der Rückgang der Verkaufszahlen der Volkswagen-Tochter Audi nimmt ein bedenkliches Tempo an. Jetzt rächen sich offenbar strategische Fehlentscheidungen der Vergangenheit.

spiegel.title: Viktoria Rader bittet nach Tod von Ehemann um Raum zum Trauern
spiegel.description: Aus bisher unbekannten Gründen stürzte L’Osteria-Mitbegründer Klaus Rader auf Mallorca mit einem Rennwagen in eine Schlucht. Nach seinem Tod bittet die Ehefrau darum, die Privatsphäre ihrer Familie zu respektieren.

spiegel.title: Bärbel Bas kündigt Rücktritt von ihren Ämtern an – Schweitzer übernimmt Ministerium
spiegel.description: In der schwarz-roten Regierung war sie bislang Arbeitsministerin, in der SPD Co-Vorsitzende. Nun gibt Bärbel Bas beide Ämter aufgrund eines Trauerfalls ab. Die Nachfolge im Kabinett steht nach SPIEGEL-Informationen bereits.

spiegel.title: Erbschaftsteuer: Familienunternehmer und DIHK gegen höhere Abgaben
spiegel.description: Zwei Tage nimmt sich der 1. Senat des Bundesverfassungsgerichts Zeit, um die Argumente für und gegen die Erbschaftsteuer anzuhören. Die Familienunternehmer machen ihre Position schon im Vorfeld klar.

spiegel.title: Kaja Kallas warnt vor Ölkatastrophe durch russische Schattenflotte
spiegel.description: Mit immer neuen Tankern bastelt Russland an einer Parallelstruktur für den globalen Ölhandel. Die maroden Schiffe werden jedoch zunehmend zum Risiko, fürchtet nun die EU-Außenbeauftragte.

spiegel.title: Versteigerung: Ein Fohlen namens J-Nimon K räumt ab
spiegel.description: Mit seiner ungewöhnlichen Fellzeichnung begeistert ein Hengstfohlen aus Brandenburg Pferdefans weltweit: J-Nimon K sieht aus wie ein Dalmatiner.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Pressestimmen zum Rennen in Singapur mit Sieger Max Verstappen
spiegel.description: In seinem 250. Grand Prix triumphiert Max Verstappen erstmals in Singapur. Die internationale Presse würdigt ihn und Kimi Antonelli, der nach Rang drei bereits in zwei Wochen Weltmeister werden kann.

spiegel.title: Nordkorea feuert laut Südkorea erneut ballistische Raketen ab
spiegel.description: Eigentlich verbietet eine Uno-Resolution Nordkorea das Abfeuern ballistischer Raketen, Machthaber Kim Jong Un bastelt dennoch weiter an seiner militärischen Stärke. Nun hat Seoul erneut Alarm gegeben.

spiegel.title: 1,4 Millionen Arbeitslose beziehen seit mindestens fünf Jahren Bürgergeld
spiegel.description: Die Zahl der Langzeitarbeitslosen, die im Bürgergeld festhängen, hat sich in den vergangenen zwei Jahren deutlich erhöht. Die AfD nutzt die Situation für eine populistische Kampagne.

spiegel.title: Linkenchef drängt auf Verbot von Zwangsräumungen, die in die Obdachlosigkeit führen
spiegel.description: Eine Rentnerin in Spanien muss aus ihrer Wohnung, die grobe Behandlung führt zu Massenprotesten. Linkenchef Pantisano nimmt sich den »Fall Maricarmen« zur Mahnung – und will neue Regeln bei Zwangsräumungen.

spiegel.title: BDI fordert mehr Abwehrbereitschaft gegen russische Sabotage
spiegel.description: Desinformation und Sabotage gehören zum versteckten Krieg Russlands gegen den Westen. Betroffen davon ist auch die Industrie. Der BDI fordert deshalb mehr Aufmerksamkeit.

observador.title: Passos Coelho quer salvar a direita ou afundar Montenegro?
observador.description: Passos quer salvar a direita aliando-se a André Ventura. Já algumas figuras políticas ainda estão a tentar perceber porque é que a subida dos juros faz cair o fundo das pensões.

observador.title: Sismo no Panamá: 1.200 casas e 419 escolas afetadas
observador.description: Dois dias após o sismo de magnitude 7,7, o Panamá contabiliza 27 feridos, sem mortos. Populações estão sem água, luz e alimentos. Governo disponibilizou 86 milhões de euros para a reconstrução.

observador.title: Seguros de saúde cada vez mais importantes no recrutamento
observador.description: Quatro em cada dez trabalhadores consideram a oferta e a cobertura de seguro de saúde determinante para aceitarem uma proposta de trabalho.

observador.title: 9h. Habitação. PSP retira tendas de protesto no Porto
observador.description: Foram mais de 50 as pessoas que pernoitaram esta noite na Praça D. João I. Ainda, Ministros dos Negócios Estrangeiros da UE aprovam hoje o maior pacote de sanções de sempre contra a Rússia.

observador.title: Habitação. Polícia retira tendas de protesto no Porto
observador.description: Mais de 50 pessoas pernoitaram na Praça D. João I desde sábado em tendas pelo direito à habitação e contra o aumento do custo de vida. Polícia desmantelou esta segunda-feira de manhã o acampamento.

observador.title: Passos: mais importante do que aquilo que disse é o que fez
observador.description: Passos Coelho (que deu uma entrevista), Mário Centeno (que é contra a descida do IRS) e José Luís Carneiro (que é contra a descida do IRC) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Pyongyang lança "projétil não identificado" no mar do Japão
observador.description: Ação surge na sequência do teste de lançamento, realizado por Seul na quinta-feira, de um veículo planador hipersónico, a primeira arma sul-coreana deste tipo fabricada no território nacional.

observador.title: Luís Montenegro é o novo bailarino do parlamento?
observador.description: Paulo Raimundo elogiou dotes de dança do primeiro-ministro enquanto Paulo Núncio atacou previsões de Mário Centeno e chamou-o de "Professor Chibanga". Ainda houve tempo para provérbios desastrosos.

observador.title: A Europa quer mais dinheiro para gastar, mas ninguém lho dá
observador.description: A Irlanda apresentou este sábado a sua proposta para o próximo quadro orçamental europeu, que vai até 2034, mas as reacções críticas antecipam uma Cimeira Europeia muito difícil. O dinheiro não chega.

observador.title: Cabo Verde. Universidade pública com propinas gratuitas
observador.description: Orçamento da UniCV cresceu de 10,8 para 16,3 milhões de euros para acomodar a gratuitidade, entre outras medidas, disse Astrigilda Silveira, que quer diversificar as fontes de receita.

observador.title: Passos protocandidato e os rendimentos de Santana
observador.description: Passos Coelho não deixou quase nada por dizer em entrevista a Maria João Avillez. Santana Lopes ganhava mais como comentador do que como autarca. Fim de semana de ataques de Trump à Ucrânia.

observador.title: 8h. Passos Coelho quer acordo à direita para reformar o país
observador.description: Os principais momentos da entrevista do antigo PM na SIC Notícias. Ainda, após anúncio do acordo entre os EUA e a Rússia para o fornecimento de diesel, os preços do petróleo já estão a mudar.

observador.title: Messi leva raspanete do Barça por falta de despedida?
observador.description: Das críticas e da azia do Barcelona a Messi à mansão de Federer inaugurada após sete anos de espera. Destaca-se também o novo título mundial da patinadora Madalena Costa.

observador.title: Até onde vai a loucura para sobreviver ao apocalipse?
observador.description: Com toneladas de comida num bunker escondido numa aldeia, um pai raptou a própria filha para salvar do fim do mundo. E agora também há uma nova moda: tomar banho passou à história.

observador.title: Barack Obama já virou uma peça de museu da política?
observador.description: O mundo mudou tanto que a era Obama parece pré-história face a Trump. E ainda, a vontade do Estado em brincar às empresas, a reeleição de António Costa na UE e os autarcas mal pagos.

observador.title: Máximas vão subir e podem chegar aos 30 graus
observador.description: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera explica que na terça e quarta-feira está prevista uma subida gradual das temperaturas, em especial a máxima, que estará acima da média para a época do ano.

observador.title: Banco Mundial. IA pode gerar emprego em países emergentes
observador.description: O presidente do Banco Mundial destacou que, nos países de pouco rendimento e de rendimento médio inferior, a oportunidade para a pequena IA gerar empregos e aumentar a produtividade é enorme.

observador.title: Setembro foi o segundo mais quente de sempre
observador.description: Dados indicam que setembro marcou o segundo mês consecutivo em 2026 com temperaturas globais superiores a 1,5ºC (graus Celsius) acima dos níveis pré-industriais.

elpais.title: Martiño Rivas: “No me sentía cómodo en la ‘Super Pop’. Ahora digo: ¿cómo no las guardé? Las tendría enmarcadas”
elpais.description: El actor gallego sigue demostrando en la serie ‘El problema final’ su versatilidad como actor y, en esta entrevista, su sentido del humor como conversador

elpais.title: ¿Para qué sirve una ciudad?
elpais.description: El ensayista Pedro Bravo, autor ‘Antes todo esto era ciudad’, charla en este videopodcast con el periodista Sergio C. Fanjul sobre el devenir de la urbe contemporánea

elpais.title: Bárbara sin Rey
elpais.description: Hasta el presente festival de Sitges nunca había escuchado a Bárbara Rey hablar de su trabajo como actriz. A mí me ha interesado mucho más

elpais.description: La solidaridad a gran escala genera comunidad y oxitocina, el catalizador más frecuente de la desobediencia civil

elpais.description:
La ultraderecha mundial dora la píldora a 
Netanyahu solo porque es mucho más despiadado (aún) que sus antecesores

elpais.title: Día de la Hispanidad y reacciones políticas en directo | Los Reyes presiden los actos de una fiesta nacional marcada por el adelanto electoral
elpais.description: Sánchez reivindica una España diversa: “Llevamos nuestros derechos por bandera”

elpais.title: Bruselas teme ataques híbridos de Rusia en el superciclo electoral europeo que se abre con España
elpais.description: Europa advierte de que el Kremlin busca desestabilizar a la UE y testar la capacidad de respuesta de la OTAN en un momento clave para el futuro del proyecto común

elpais.title: Burnham acusa directamente a Rusia de interferir en la campaña del referéndum del Brexit
elpais.description: Es la primera vez que Downing Street señala a Moscú por este asunto. El primer ministro advierte del peligro a Alemania y Francia

elpais.description: Las heridas históricas, la polarización política y la desinformación erosionan el apoyo social a los desplazados por la guerra

nyt.title: Saudi and Yemeni Airports Hit in New Round of Strikes
nyt.description: At least one person was killed in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, kingdom authorities said. The Houthis said Saudi aircraft hit the Yemeni capital’s airport.

nyt.title: Saudi Arabia Has Few Options as Houthis Aim at Heart of Its Ambitions
nyt.description: Three deadly attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen on an airport in the Saudi capital underscored the asymmetrical nature of their conflict with the kingdom.

nyt.title: An Israeli Election Like No Other
nyt.description: Many say a vote in two weeks may be the most consequential in Israel’s history.

nyt.title: Can a Democrat Beat Darline Graham? 5 Takeaways From the South Carolina Senate Debate
nyt.description: Dr. Annie Andrews, the Democratic challenger, accused Senator Darline Graham of taking her cues from President Trump. Ms. Graham said Dr. Andrews wouldn’t say no to socialists.

nyt.title: The Taliban Are Using Europe’s Fear of Migrants to Their Advantage
nyt.description: European nations that condemn the Taliban government for its human rights record are seeking its help to deport refugees back to Afghanistan.

nyt.title: In Canada’s Arctic, a New Generation of Inuit Creatives Are Using Identity to Fuel Their Art
nyt.description: In Iqaluit, the only city in Canada’s Arctic, a new generation of Inuit writers and artists is turning questions of language, land and identity into books, films and even tattoos.

nyt.title: Wringing Hope From the Rubble of Gaza
nyt.description: The cease-fire last October ostensibly brought an end to Israel’s war in Gaza after the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023. A year later, however, Israeli strikes, though less frequent, haven’t stopped.

nyt.title: Mamdani to Skip Columbus Day Parade. Some Italian Americans Are Glad.
nyt.description: City Hall confirmed that the mayor would not join Monday’s procession up Fifth Avenue, but would host an Italian American heritage reception soon.

nyt.title: Russell Brand’s Rape and Sexual Assault Trial: What to Know
nyt.description: The YouTuber, comedian and actor’s trial began on Monday. He has pleaded not guilty to all of the charges.

nyt.title: Hurricane Isaias’s Aftermath in Video and Pictures
nyt.description: It was the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, and the first to hit the mainland United States in two years.

nyt.title: Flamingos at a Florida Zoo Rode Out Hurricane Isaias in the Bathroom
nyt.description: ZooWorld in Panama City Beach, Fla. squeezed a group of 30 flamingos into a bathroom to shelter them from Hurricane Isaias, which hit the Gulf Coast.

nyt.title: Waves From Powerful Storm Pound Beach Homes in Southern California
nyt.description: Waves from Post-Tropical Storm Rachel crashed into beachfront homes in Long Beach, Calif. over the weekend, prompting evacuations.

nyt.title: Hurricane Simon and Post-Tropical Storm Rachel Bring Flood Risks to Mexico and Southwestern U.S.
nyt.description: Hurricane Simon was hugging the west coast of Mexico on Sunday, while the remnants of Post-Tropical Storm Rachel churned inland, bringing heavy rain and high winds.

nyt.title: ‘It’s the Identity, Stupid!’: 3 Writers on Europe’s Rising Far Right
nyt.description: A discussion on the roots of the far-right’s success, its plans for power and what President Trump has to do with it all.

nyt.title: Meet Sanyi, the Rooster That United a Hungarian Town
nyt.description: A Hungarian town, an escaped rooster and the universal longing for freedom.

npr.title: Hundreds detained in voter roll protests in India
npr.description: Protesters in the Indian capital have again defied authorities to demonstrate against a controversial revision of the country's voter rolls that has seen 130 million people removed, or threatened with removal.

npr.title: Deadly Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia raise stakes for US
npr.description: The deadliest attack on a Gulf Arab state since the Iran war began has heightened concerns that the United States could become directly involved in another regional conflict.

npr.title: Trump says Russia and Ukraine agree to an 'energy ceasefire'
npr.description: President Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire," but he offered no details on it and Kyiv reported attacks by Moscow on energy sites after his statement.

npr.title: Seafarer's union official says crews offered big money to transit Strait of Hormuz
npr.description: As attacks continue to mount on shipping vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a seafarer's union official says some crews are being offered big rewards for making the crossing.

npr.title: Harrowing accounts of violence and sex abuse in women's prison told in new podcast
npr.description: Madi Bolanos and Anna Sussman's new podcast We Are Jane Doe, by KQED and Snap Studios, investigates rampant sex abuse at the Central California Women's Facility in Chowchilla, Ca.

npr.title: Ukrainian MP calls U.S.-Russia diesel deal a 'betrayal'
npr.description: NPR's Joel Rose speaks with Ukrainian Minister of Parliament, Oleksandr Merezhko, about the U.S.'s diesel deal with Russia will impact Ukraine.

npr.title: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery this week
npr.description: Pope Leo XIV said he would undergo surgery after doctors found a "localized nodule" in his lung.

npr.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
npr.description: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?

npr.title: Saudi airport passenger terminal is struck again, a day after 12 were killed
npr.description: A projectile struck a passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh on Sunday, a day after a missile hit the same terminal and killed 12 people, officials said.

npr.title: Bayeux Tapestry's London tour spurs enthusiasts to Battle of Hastings reenactment
npr.description: A reenactment of the Battle of Hastings, which took place almost a millennium ago, is drawing crowds of enthusiasts in the UK.

republika.description: Internista con esperienza nell'emergenza-urgenza e al Gemelli, guida la sanità vaticana e seguirà il Pontefice durante l'intervento per la rimozione del nodulo al polmone

republika.description: A new map of the Roman Empire’s road network charts 300,000 kilometres of routes. Archaeologist Tom Brughmans: “Many of our stereotypes come from looking at the Appian Way. But not every road was straight, and many cities were better connected than the capital.”

phys-org.description: New research led by Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and published in the journal Earth System Dynamics shows a clear warming signal across the Congo Basin since the 1960s, using historical weather records from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). These records come from the paper archives of the Institut National pour l'Etude et la Recherche Agronomiques (INERA) in Yangambi, DRC, and the State Archives of Belgium.

phys-org.title: Wildlife populations have declined 73% since 1970—but many of the world's animals still aren't being counted
phys-org.description: Wildlife populations around the world have declined by an average of 73% since 1970. That's according to the WWF's new 2026 Living Planet Index—a major estimate, updated every two years, of the changing state of nature. This does not mean that 73% of the world's animals have disappeared. Rather, it is the average decline in the size of wildlife populations being monitored.

phys-org.title: 'DNA Typewriter' records cells' history in developing mouse embryo
phys-org.description: Scientists have succeeded in reconstructing the family tree of cells in a developing mouse embryo. They recorded cells' relationships, starting when the fertilized egg first split in two and ending after the body and its organs took shape. That period lasted 13.5 days. (Full gestation in mice is 19 to 21 days.)

phys-org.title: Quantum 'birthmarks' hold lasting traces of a system's past
phys-org.description: Some classical physical systems can explore many configurations over time until their long-term behavior no longer reveals their starting conditions. The sampling of available configurations according to the appropriate statistical distribution is a property called ergodicity.

phys-org.title: New study shows effects of hypoxia in Florida's Banana River
phys-org.description: A new study by Florida Tech assistant professor of marine sciences Austin Fox, Ph.D. '15, found that low oxygen levels are contributing to the rerelease of nutrients buried on the river floor that feed harmful algal blooms. The study was based on the most widespread testing ever of oxygen levels across the Banana River.

phys-org.title: At least 4 dead as cyclone Isaias drenches southern U.S.
phys-org.description: Four people died in the southeastern United States as post-tropical cyclone Isaias posed flooding and tornado risks Saturday as it moved northward after making landfall on Florida's Gulf Coast.

phys-org.title: Jurassic fossil reveals ancient origins of how mammals drink milk
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers has uncovered new evidence illuminating the evolutionary origins of one of the defining features of mammals: the ability to suckle and consume milk during infancy. Their findings, published in Nature, suggest that key anatomical structures required for mammalian suckling, swallowing and breastfeeding behaviors evolved nearly 165 million years ago, long before the appearance of modern mammals.

phys-org.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens as it nears western Mexico
phys-org.description: Hurricane Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm and was expected to make landfall or skirt the coast of west-central Mexico on Sunday, according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center.

phys-org.title: South Korea completes trial of Arctic shipping route
phys-org.description: A South Korean container ship returned on Sunday from a trial voyage through the Arctic, testing an alternative route opened by melting sea ice as conflict in the Middle East disrupts global shipping.

phys-org.title: Egypt's Fayoum mummy portraits to travel abroad for first time after restoration
phys-org.description: Egypt unveiled Sunday a restored version of the "Tondo of the Two Brothers," a prized second-century painting from the famed Fayoum portraits.

phys-org.title: New algorithm could predict Arctic sea ice up to 9 months ahead, offering new climate insights
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Mubadala Arabian Center for Climate and Environmental Sciences (ACCESS) at NYU Abu Dhabi have developed a new algorithm that can forecast Arctic sea ice extent up to nine months in advance, offering a new way to anticipate changes in the Arctic that can affect the global climate system. The research is published in the journal Scientific Reports.

phys-org.title: Spinach nanoparticles help failing rat hearts via 'borrowed photosynthesis'
phys-org.description: A spinach leaf can turn light into chemical energy. A struggling heart cannot. Researchers in China have brought part of the leaf's energy-making machinery into rat heart cells to test whether borrowed photosynthesis could help an overworked heart.

phys-org.title: Zimbabwe's dinosaurs were different from South Africa's: New species offers clues
phys-org.description: Africa boasts up to 25% of Earth's animal and plant species. This diversity is driven by varied habitats: harsh deserts, vast grasslands, dense forests, towering mountains, lush coastlines and teeming seas. It is also due to deep evolutionary roots, as many animal and plant groups originated here in the distant past. Paleontologists have been excavating this material for nearly two centuries.

phys-org.title: Ultraviolet laser pulses engineer diamond defects selectively, leaving quantum qubits intact
phys-org.description: When we think about a diamond, we often think about a material whose value comes from its perfection. In my research, however, I am interested in something almost opposite: the tiny imperfections inside diamonds. These atomic-scale defects can give diamonds new optical and electronic properties, and some of them can serve as quantum systems. The challenge is learning how to control these defects without disturbing the others.

phys-org.title: How to meal prep safely: A microbiologist's step‑by‑step guide
phys-org.description: Meal prepping is a great way to save money, spend less time in the kitchen and stick to a meal plan. But while cooking meals for the week ahead may be convenient, there can be real risks associated with eating bulk-cooked meals.

phys-org.description: As a teenager, Gillian Maegan Montalbo's pimples weren't too bad—just a few bumps on her forehead and nose.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

proj-syn.title: A Global Economic Recovery Built on Shaky Foundations
proj-syn.description: The latest update of the Brookings-FT TIGER survey reveals that global growth has stabilized, with both advanced and emerging market economies showing positive momentum. But amid persistent inflation and fiscal profligacy, policymakers will still be forced to push forward with structural reforms to unleash productivity growth.

proj-syn.title: The French Far Right Embraces Austerity
proj-syn.description: In a recent speech detailing her economic program, the French far-right leader Marine Le Pen offered what can only be described as a populist vision of fiscal consolidation. Whether she can make such a paradoxical formulation work will now determine her own future, and possibly that of Europe’s nationalist right.

proj-syn.title: Rating Africa on Its Own Terms
proj-syn.description: For decades, African countries' borrowing costs have been largely determined by major credit-rating agencies whose methods overlook key features of these economies' institutions and markets. The new Africa Credit Rating Agency could mark a turning point, challenging how the continent’s credit risk is graded and priced.

proj-syn.title: Development Finance Needs More Than One Currency
proj-syn.description: For many developing countries, renminbi-denominated loans offer a credible, increasingly accessible, and cost-effective alternative to borrowing in dollars. Now that the stability and predictability of US economic policies and institutions are in question, the Chinese currency is becoming more attractive.

proj-syn.title: Mélenchon Is Right About France’s Debt
proj-syn.description: When, in the name of moderation, centrists brand every sensible alternative to severe austerity as “nonsense,” they leave voters only one electable rebellion on offer, and the far right is happy to supply it. That is what is happening in France today.

proj-syn.title: Fukuyama, Thiel, and the Revenge of the Last Man
proj-syn.description: In his new memoir, Francis Fukuyama attempts to redeem his thesis about the end of history. But Peter Thiel’s ongoing quest to escape government oversight and wrest control of the future from democratic majorities makes a mockery of his argument all over again.

proj-syn.title: The Journalists’ Revolt Against AI Scraping
proj-syn.description: Big Tech’s oligopolistic dominance has prevented the news industry from developing a sustainable business model for the digital age—a crisis that AI is exacerbating. To preserve this important pillar of democracy, the Spanish-language publisher Editorial Perfil is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Self-Destructive Culture War
proj-syn.description: Polls suggest that MAGA fanaticism might not be playing so well outside US President Donald Trump’s loyal base. But if the Democrats want to retake one or both chambers of Congress, they should concentrate on the economy and not answer Republican extremism with a culture war of their own.

proj-syn.title: How to Break the German Malaise
proj-syn.description: For too long, Germany’s political and corporate elite coasted on the country’s postwar economic and political success story, avoiding difficult but necessary reforms that could have kept extremist populist parties at bay. Now that the barbarians are at the gates, mainstream elites must rethink everything.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Place in the Global Redivision of Labor
proj-syn.description: While the US continues to lead in software, some high-tech sectors, and hydrocarbons, China is becoming increasingly competitive in many high-tech, capital-intensive sectors, not least those once dominated by Europe. The EU does have a relative advantage in this new economic order, if only its leaders would recognize it.

proj-syn.title: The World Has Passed Peak Trump
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump, previously the most powerful, unpredictable force on the international stage, has now passed the peak of his ability to disrupt the international order. With his approval ratings collapsing, foreign leaders whose tenures will extend beyond his own are starting to write him off.

proj-syn.title: Global Financial Reform that Centers African Women
proj-syn.description: While gender-equality objectives often fall by the wayside in times of upheaval, the current rupture in the multilateral order creates an opportunity to build a debt architecture that will deliver for the women of Africa. The first steps toward this goal can be taken at this month’s IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

proj-syn.title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
proj-syn.description: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

proj-syn.title: Closing NATO’s Deterrence Gap
proj-syn.description: With Russian provocations against NATO member states growing more frequent, the alliance urgently needs to develop a credible doctrine of punitive deterrence to guide its response to acts of aggression that fall below the threshold of war. Mere territorial defense is not enough.

proj-syn.title: The India-Pakistan Cold War
proj-syn.description: The current stalemate between India and Pakistan should be viewed not as a pause between rounds of negotiation, but rather as part of a deliberate Indian strategy of disengagement. India will return to the negotiating table only after Pakistan dismantles, comprehensively and verifiably, its state-supported terrorist networks.

proj-syn.title: The Next Era of Reform Must Be About Capability
proj-syn.description: Economic development should no longer be measured solely by how much finance is mobilized or how much fiscal space is created. It must also be judged by whether countries emerge more capable of setting their own priorities, responding to challenges, and seizing new opportunities to shape their own future.

proj-syn.title: With AI, Sharing Is Caring
proj-syn.description: Although the public's distrust of Big Tech is understandable, given past experience, that is not a reason to starve AI models of the information and data they will need to be useful. If serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on the technology's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.

proj-syn.title: Why the US-China Trade Truce Matters
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump’s agreement to extend their trade truce reflects the fact that both sides have leverage over the other. In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, the current fragile equilibrium may be the best one can hope for.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI And Energy Top A Busy Lineup Of Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: As the AI startup boom progresses, investors appear to be leaving few niches unfunded. That was apparent in this week’s lineup of large funding rounds, which featured AI infrastructure providers, a foundational model developer, a content protection platform for the AI age, and other AI-focused startups among the top investment recipients.

crunchbase.description: Active startup investors largely kept up or increased their dealmaking pace in the third quarter, even as overall venture funding declined with the absence of new record megarounds for AI leaders.

crunchbase.title: Why Customer Workflows Are Becoming The Moat In The AI Era
crunchbase.description: AI companies can build durable moats by embedding their products in essential customer workflows, explains tech adviser Itay Sagie, who shares why founders should prioritize measurable customer dependence, while investors and acquirers should assess how integrations, trusted relationships and workflow access can strengthen retention and drive growth.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Gudea Lands $7M To Predict Which Online Narratives Will Go Viral

crunchbase.title: Europe Posted Its Strongest Quarter In Q3 In 4 Years, As Its Venture Ecosystem Expands Beyond The UK
crunchbase.description: European startup funding reached $25 billion last quarter, well above the $14 billion invested in Q3 2025 and up slightly from the $24 billion invested in Q2. Quarterly funding was up 77% year over year, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: From Ballet To Breach Prevention: How A Magician’s Son Raised $4.2M In Seed Funding For His Cybersecurity Startup
crunchbase.description: The latest in our series of articles on venture funding to non-tech founders features a former magician's assistant and ballet dancer who's building cybersecurity software with $4.2 million in seed funding.

crunchbase.title: There Was Never An Easy AI Era, And Investors Are Raising The Bar
crunchbase.description: As AI IPOs bring greater scrutiny, argues guest author Maor Farid, founder and CEO of Leo AI, investors will increasingly prioritize customer spending growth, sustainable margins and deployment efficiency over rapid revenue growth alone.

crunchbase.title: North America’s Startup Funding Falls In Q3 As AI Giants Eye The Public Markets
crunchbase.description: In total, investors poured $92 billion into seed- through growth-stage rounds for U.S. and Canadian startups in the third quarter, per Crunchbase data. That’s a 35% decline from the prior quarter but up 50% from year-ago levels.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows AI’s Most Active Startups Are Becoming Serial Acquirers
crunchbase.description: Some of the AI industry’s fastest-growing startups are becoming serial acquirers, buying smaller companies to fill product gaps, enter new markets and bring specialized teams in-house, a review of Crunchbase data shows. While AI giant OpenAI is by far the busiest of these buyers, well-funded startups in legal tech, customer service and software development have also made multiple acquisitions this year.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows. And while the third quarter was the lowest for startup investment so far this year, it still exceeded every other quarter since Q2 2022. We take a look at where the funding went.
